items.title: ISO members send net-zero draft back for revisions
items.summary: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) is reviewing suggested changes to its corporate net-zero standard after a vote on the first draft fell short of the approval threshold.

items.title: How UK is moving climate security up the international agenda
items.summary: The package includes £330m for the Global Environment Facility, the main global multilateral fund for protecting nature and tackling environmental threats.

items.title: UK’s largest dairy farms face calls for tighter environmental controls
items.summary: The Wildlife Trusts is calling for policy reform to bring the most intensive dairy operations under stronger environmental regulation, after research found that more than 40-mega dairies are not subjected to the same level of monitoring as intensive pig and poultry units.

items.title: Germany unveils roadmap to quit fossil fuels by 2045
items.summary: At the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, Germany announced its roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels "no later than 2045".

items.title: NEXT WEEK: What does a revised ISO 14001 mean for sustainability professionals?
items.summary: On 29 September, edie is hosting a webinar in partnership with BSI to explore changes to the ISO 14001 standard addressing environmental management.

items.title: Saving $500m a year: The business case for regenerative agriculture
items.summary: With climate risks intensifying, global agrifood supply chains face a host of growing threats and potentially millions in lost yields.

items.title: ISO net-zero standard stalls following member feedback
items.summary: After attracting nearly 5,000 comments, members have sent the International Organization for Standardization's (ISO's) proposed standard back for revisions.

items.title: Interactive: What China’s dozens of ‘five-year plans’ say about climate and energy
items.summary: Five-year plans are an important part of China’s policymaking process, signalling key priorities and setting targets for the coming years.

items.title: Analysis: EVs are now nine times cheaper than petrol or diesel to drive in the UK
items.summary: The latest surge in fossil-fuel prices means it is now up to nine times cheaper in the UK to drive an electric vehicle (EV) than a petrol or diesel car, shows Carbon Brief analysis.
